acceptanceCriteria: Per-role escalation follows consecutive native no-progress sessions, resets on progress and supports per-tier caps without unsupported model configuration.
Status/events expose current tier and streak; top-tier typed operator requests integrate with the accepted escalation channel.
Required contract, independent review, focused qualification, CEM/OCM, current-main integration and native completion/readback/audit are retained.
body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/499; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Some tickets make no progress for many consecutive sessions on the default model, while a stronger model would likely finish them. Today the operator watches the event log and hand-edits roles. We built this in an external work-state script, but the dispatcher is where it belongs.

## Request
A role-level escalation ladder keyed on consecutive no-progress sessions per ticket:
```json
"roles": [{"name": "matrix-worker", "model": "A", "escalate": [{"after": 3, "model": "B"}, {"after": 6, "model": "C", "notes": "operator-visible"}], "deescalateOnProgress": true}]
```
- Count trailing `finished ... no progress` sessions per ticket from the dispatcher's own events; any progress resets it.
- Surface the current tier and streak in `dispatch status`, emit an `escalated` event, and let a worker at the top tier attach a typed NEEDS-OPERATOR request (see the escalation request).
- Per-tier caps so a stronger, scarcer model is not flooded.

## Workaround in use
`workState` returns `t1-`/`t2-` prefixed states and duplicate roles per tier (cap 1 each, separate role-claim slots).

title: Feature: dispatch model-escalation ladder keyed on consecutive no-progress sessions
